entry.title: Internship at NIMS, Japan
entry.content:
This month I’ve started a 3-month internship at the National Institute for Materials Science (NIMS) in Tsukuba, Japan 🇯🇵.

Over the coming months, I’ll be getting hands-on experience with their state-of-the-art TEM facilities. This is an amazing opportunity to dive deeper into microscopy and pick up skills I wouldn’t get anywhere else, pushing my research further in the final year of my PhD.

I’m grateful for the support from the University of Bristol and the Bristol Composites Institute in making this possible, and I’m excited to see where this experience takes me!

National Institute for Materials Science, Tsukuba
entry.summary: Starting a 3-month internship in Tsukuba, Japan at NIMS to gain hands-on experience with TEM.

entry.title: Recognised as Associate Fellow of Advance HE

link.title: Recognised as Associate Fellow of Advance HE

entry.content:
I’ve been awarded the status of Associate Fellow of Advance HE (AFHEA) — formerly known as the Higher Education Academy.

This professional recognition reflects my engagement with teaching and learning support in higher education. I’m especially pleased that my portfolio was also nominated for an Outstanding Portfolio Award.

Teaching has always been an important part of my academic life. Would I have pursued science if it weren’t for the inspiring teachers I had growing up? Probably not. That experience continues to shape how I teach today — especially in supporting students from international or neurodivergent backgrounds.

A heartfelt thank you to Karen Parrish, Amy McCarty Torrens, and Rebekah Jeans — the champions of teaching at the School of Chemistry, University of Bristol. Your encouragement, feedback, and high standards pushed me to reflect deeply and improve my practice.

This milestone wouldn’t have happened without your support.

Certificate of recognition: Associate Fellow of Advance HE (AFHEA).
entry.summary: I've been awarded Associate Fellowship of Advance HE (AFHEA), with my portfolio nominated for an Outstanding Portfolio Award.

entry.title: New Paper in RSC Advances — Biotemplated Superconductors

link.title: New Paper in RSC Advances — Biotemplated Superconductors

entry.content:
Our newest paper has just been published in RSC Advances:
“Morphological control of cuprate superconductors using sea sponges as templates.”

In this study, we explored a greener approach to superconductor synthesis by using natural sea sponges as a sustainable biotemplate, leveraging their intrinsic 3D architecture to produce porous YBCO and BSCCO superconductors.

This work was a collaborative effort with my brilliant friend and co-author Jula Carlotta Schroeder, and with the guidance of my supervisors Simon Hall, Stephen Eichhorn, and Avinash Patil.

You can read the full article here: https://doi.org/10.1039/d5ra00541h

All of my publications are available in the Publications tab.

SEM micrograph showing the transition from natural spongin fibres to porous YBCO structure after biotemplated synthesis.
entry.summary: Our latest paper on sustainable superconductor synthesis using sea sponges is now out in RSC Advances!

entry.title: NTREM 2025 — Best Oral Presentation Award
entry.content:
I recently had the honour of attending the 27th New Trends in Research of Energetic Materials (NTREM) conference in Pardubice, Czech Republic.

During the event, I presented my research titled:

“Novel explosive method for the synthesis of silver nanoparticles.”

I’m delighted to share that I was awarded 1st place for Best Oral Presentation. The conference brought together researchers from across academia and industry, and it was a pleasure to take part in such a vibrant exchange of ideas.

Congratulations to Marcin Gerlich as well, who received Best Poster Presentation for his excellent work.

On stage with Jiri Pachman, Marcin Gerlich and Adam Cumming during the award ceremony.
Best Oral Presentation — Diploma from NTREM 2025.
Group photo of NTREM 2025 attendees.
entry.summary: Attending NTREM 2025 and receiving the Best Oral Presentation award.

entry.title: Gold LEAF Certification for Our Lab

link.title: Gold LEAF Certification for Our Lab

entry.content:
I’m proud to share that the lab I manage has achieved Gold LEAF Certification for our commitment to improving sustainability in research. Over the past few months, I led this initiative, working closely with the team to adopt greener lab practices—from reducing energy usage and single-use plastics to improving recycling and resource efficiency.

This milestone reflects a real team effort, and I’m incredibly grateful to have worked alongside such dedicated colleagues: Michaela Whitehurst, Yutong Shen, and Krystof Chrappova. Their enthusiasm and support made this possible.

We’ll continue striving for even greater sustainability in our lab and hope to inspire others to do the same.

Gold-level certification awarded by the LEAF programme.
entry.summary: Celebrating our lab's achievement in sustainability!

entry.title: SEM Training
entry.content:
Today I continued my EM training. This time I took on SEM, a technique I haven’t spent much time on previously. With my current work focusing more on superconductors I am looking into the topography of templated samples and their composition using EDAX.

YBCO 123 prepared using waste plastic as a template.
